title: Introduce RBAC policy linter, dry-run UI and audit-sampling enforcer
author: Priya Nair
description: Context: customers and SRE teams asked for safer RBAC policy rollouts and lower-noise audit telemetry in large orgs. This PR adds a server-side RBAC policy linter, a Console dry-run toggle so operators can preview the effect of policy changes without committing enforcement, and an audit-sampling enforcer that reduces event volume while preserving key forensic signals. Motivation: reduce rollback incidents during RBAC changes, cut audit ingestion costs for high-volume tenants, and give platform engineers a clear safety net when evolving policy templates. What this PR does: 1) policy/linter: new rule engine (yaml-based rules) that validates for common misconfigurations (wildcard service principals, overly broad role bindings, missing residency constraints) and surfaces human-friendly messages; 2) api: /rbac/lint endpoint and server-side pre-merge check that runs as a GitHub App webhook and as a CI guard; 3) console: dry-run UI component and an admin toggle that wires to a new server flag so teams can preview effective decisions per-request without mutating enforcement state; 4) audit/sampler: lightweight pipeline stage that applies tenant-configurable sampling profiles (preserve-error/deny traces, sample allow events down to target rate, keep burst windows); 5) KMS tag checks: the linter now includes optional policy checks that verify KMS key tags and region attributes on bindings to catch residency-policy regressions; 6) docs and runbooks: new docs/rbac-lint.md and an incident runbook describing steps to convert a dry-run to enforcement and how to interpret sampler metrics. Testing and rollout: unit + integration tests added for the rule engine, nightly e2e against an internal staging cluster, and a gradual rollout gated by a feature flag with a canary cohort (10% tenant traffic) for two weeks before global enablement. Backwards compatibility: dry-run is read-only by default and does not change enforcement until flipped by admins; sampling defaults to pass-through for existing tenants unless a profile is specified. Checklist: - [x] add linter engine and server endpoint - [x] wire GitHub App CI integration - [x] Console UI + admin toggle - [x] audit sampler pipeline and metrics - [x] KMS tag validators (opt-in) - [x] docs and runbook - [x] tests and CI coverage - [x] staged rollout plan and monitoring hooks Related: linear ENG-2107 and SEC-332; support ticket SUP-4421.
commit_summary: Initial commit: policy linter implementation and rule set; API: add rbac/lint controller and webhook handler; Console: PolicyDryRunToggle component and toggle backend; Audit: sampler stage and prometheus metrics; Docs: rbac-lint.md + runbook; Tests: unit + integration + e2e; CI: add rbac-lint workflow.
review_conversation: Reviewer Ethan: asked for clearer errors when multiple bindings overlap; requested tests for residency check edge-cases. Author reply: added overlap detection and a new test matrix. Reviewer Marcus: requested e2e that validates sampling preserves deny traces; added an integration test and a prometheus rule. Reviewer Ana: recommended UX copy update and a tooltip for the dry-run toggle; console copy updated and UX reviewed. All reviewers approved after two follow-ups; final merge after CI green. The conversation included one transient CI failure on e2e which was rerun and passed.
release_notes: Added RBAC policy linter with server-side checks; introduced Console dry-run for policy previews; added audit-sampling enforcer to reduce high-volume telemetry while preserving deny/error traces; optional KMS tag checks to catch residency misconfigurations; feature gated with staged rollout.
notes_on_rollout: Rollout plan: enable feature flag in staging for one week, then enable for 10% tenant traffic via canary (region-aware), monitor sampler metrics (audit.rate, audit.sampled_rate, rbac.lint.errors) and Console usage telemetry; if errors or anomaly spikes occur revert flag and open incident. Post-rollout: schedule a follow-up to extend rule-set based on live violations.
safety_considerations: Dry-run mode is read-only and must not alter enforcement state; linter warnings do not block enforcement unless configured in policy profiles. Audit sampler preserves all deny/critical audit events and keeps a deterministic subset of allows to ensure reproducibility for forensic needs.
